summary: The retained specimen results correctly implement a descriptive omission sensitivity over technical-valid reconstructed tracks using the explicitly disclosed `projection_z_extent_um` field. Independent recomputation from the content-bound replay archive exactly reproduced both specimens' counts, fractions, length medians, and representative-width medians. Short tracks remain in the primary population, and the sensitivity output is confined to technical QC. Acceptance remains blocked because missing/nonfinite track lengths are not handled safely by the production aggregate writer, and focused tests do not cover this adversarial case or the exact 2.0-um/rounding boundary.

findings.title: Nonfinite track length can silently invalidate the specimen count partition
findings.impact: A technical-valid track with missing or nonnumeric `projection_z_extent_um` is counted in the primary denominator but in neither omission category. The production aggregate writer can therefore emit internally inconsistent counts and an understated below-2-um fraction instead of explicitly failing or reporting unavailable sensitivity.

findings.recommendation: Before calculating sensitivity, require every technical-valid track to have a finite, nonnegative `projection_z_extent_um`; fail the sensitivity calculation with a clear QC status or report missing-length counts explicitly. Add an adversarial test proving the chosen behavior.

findings.title: The exact 2.0-um and pre-threshold rounding behavior lacks regression coverage
findings.impact: Lengths are rounded to 0.001 um before the track-level threshold is applied. Objects geometrically just below 2 um can therefore be classified with the `>=2.0` subset, and no test fixes the intended stored-value semantics or exact-boundary behavior.

findings.recommendation: Add synthetic cases at 1.9994, 1.9996, exactly 2.0, and 2.0004 um. Either apply the threshold to unrounded calibrated geometry or explicitly document and test that classification uses the stored rounded `projection_z_extent_um`.

findings.title: The sensitivity length is a projection-plus-Z extent, not anatomical length
findings.impact: The calculation quantifies sensitivity to a specific calibrated apparent-extent definition. It does not establish true 3D centerline length, distinguish genuine short nuclei from fragments, or establish biological identity or anatomical organ volume.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as requested.

Focused pytest execution was blocked by the read-only environment's lack of a writable temporary directory; conclusions use static test inspection, commit-bound artifacts, and an independent read-only replay recomputation.
The retained replay covers two included specimens. It verifies computation and provenance, not population-wide biological validity or group effects.
This review does not establish whether any individual below-2-um track is a genuine nucleus rather than an unresolved fragment or terminal optical section.
recommended_follow_up: Make missing/nonfinite `projection_z_extent_um` handling explicit and add an adversarial regression test.
